claims.text: Equiatomic FeCoNi has an fcc structure, high saturation magnetization, and low coercivity.
Replacing approximately 20–25 at.% of a FeCoNi base component with Tb can produce a near-equiatomic FeCoNiTb alloy.
The proposed FeCoNiTb composition has configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
The Tb-modified alloy can remain single phase under standard synthesis and annealing protocols.
Localized Tb 4f electrons provide strong spin–orbit coupling.
Introducing Tb into FeCoNi will enhance magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Strong spin–orbit coupling, when combined with suitable low-symmetry chemical or crystal structure, facilitates strong magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy enhances domain-wall pinning.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning produces a higher coercive field.
FeCoNiTb will have significantly higher coercivity than equiatomic FeCoNi.
FeCoNiTb will have significantly higher coercivity than the prior FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives.
The Tb-modified alloy will maintain high saturation magnetization.
FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt exhibit low coercivity and soft-ferromagnetic behavior despite high saturation magnetization.
The coercivity enhancement should remain observable during ambient-temperature measurements when synthesis and annealing treatments are held identical.
Rare-earth substitution has previously enhanced magnetic anisotropy in related alloy systems.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant coercivity increase exceeding 20% relative to FeCoNi is specified as the falsification criterion.

contradictions.description: A literal replacement of 20–25 atomic-percentage points from only one component of equiatomic FeCoNi would leave that component at roughly 8–13 at.% while Fe and Co or their equivalents remain near 33 at.%, which is not an almost equiatomic quaternary composition. The intended final composition is therefore ambiguous.

The central prediction asserts superiority over FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but the proposed experiment includes only FeCoNi as a control. Its stated rule therefore cannot decisively establish or falsify the comparison with both prior derivatives.
